references.text: Leah praised the Lord when she gave birth to Judah – the wordplay between the name Judah (yehudah) and praise (yodukha) in 49:8 is built on this
Continuation of the blessing: The scepter shall not depart from Judah, which expands on the leadership role described in verse 8
Moses' blessing of Judah – a prayer that the Lord hears Judah's voice and leads him to victory
Judah became the most powerful among his brothers, and from him came the prince – a direct fulfillment that his brothers shall praise him
Jesus' genealogy shows that He descends from Judah, who received the prominent role among the brothers
Jesus, from the tribe of Judah, is our high priest – Judah was the tribe the Lord chose, as 49:8 predicts
Jesus is called the lion of the tribe of Judah – the ultimate fulfillment of Judah's supremacy among the brothers
A direct literary parallel where Isaac's blessing to Jacob (which includes Judah) is confirmed and specified in Jacob's own blessing to Judah.
A clear thematic parallel and possible prophetic fulfillment: The promise of victory over enemies in Gen 49:8 is resumed and strengthened in Mic 5:8.
Theological expansion: The local submission in Gen 49:8 foreshadows the global recognition and service from kings in Isa 49:23.
